title: Isolated Downstream Validation and Single‑Repair Effects in Intent‑to‑Configuration NetOps: A Preregistered Paired Study
abstract: We report a preregistered paired confirmatory experiment (study cand-003-stud-001) that isolates purely downstream deterministic validation plus a bounded single-repair intervention under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Using 1,000 deterministic intents from a synthetic workflow stress corpus and a deterministic digital‑twin validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5), exactly one sampled initial generation per task was deterministically reused by both arms; any paired outcome difference therefore arises only from the deterministic validator decision and at most one permitted repair call (guarded arm). Observed outcomes: baseline safe‑deploy = 995/1000 = 0.995; guarded safe‑deploy = 1000/1000 = 1.000; discordants n10 = 5 (guarded only), n01 = 0 (baseline only); preregistered primary test exact two‑sided McNemar p = 0.0625 (not < 0.05). Preregistered paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.001, 0.01]. Total hosted model calls recorded = 1,005 (1,000 shared initial + 5 repair). We present the exact McNemar as the confirmatory inference, the bootstrap interval as a preregistered descriptive summary, and interpret the small absolute guarded benefit in light of sparse discordant counts, ceiling effects, validator scope, and the shared_initial_candidate design.

sections.introduction:
Automating translation from operator intent to device configuration promises operational gains but also introduces safety risks: incorrect command ordering, transient invariant violations, and unauthorized touches of protected fields can convert plausible plans into damaging live changes. A substantial body of work documents LLM hallucination, prompt sensitivity, and structured‑output failures that reduce correctness in code- and config-like generation and motivates verifier-augmented architectures that detect and sometimes repair unsafe outputs [1],[2].

This study answers a narrowly specified causal question recommended by that prior literature: when the generator's initial candidate is fixed, what marginal safety return does a deterministic digital‑twin validator combined with a single permitted repair call provide? We operationalize this as the paired estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline computed on complete pairs under generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate. Under these semantics baseline is the single‑shot/initial validity of the shared candidate and guarded is the final validity after deterministic validation and up to one repair. Because the same initial sampled candidate is reused deterministically for both arms, any paired outcome difference can only arise from deterministic validator decisions and the single allowed repair.

Contributions. (1) A preregistered paired confirmatory study (Npairs = 1,000) that enforces shared_initial_candidate semantics and deterministic task selection from a synthetic NetOps workflow stress corpus. (2) Full execution accounting with recorded model calls and archived validator traces; explicit reporting that model configuration recorded temperature = null/unset (null/unset is not evidence of deterministic hosted‑model sampling and does not imply temperature = 0). (3) Transparent reporting of the preregistered confirmatory test (exact two‑sided McNemar, p = 0.0625), the preregistered paired bootstrap descriptive summary (95% percentile CI = [0.001, 0.01], 10,000 resamples, seed = 1729), and an evidence‑grounded interpretation that accounts for sparse discordant counts, near‑unity baseline, and validator scope.
sections.related_work:
Empirical evaluations of LLMs for structured-generation tasks repeatedly find sensitivity to prompts and decoding, with material rates of syntactic and semantic errors that affect executability [3],[4]. Two broad mitigation families have emerged: (a) enforceable constraints at decode time (constrained/schema-aware decoding) and (b) post‑generation verification and repair. Method development work in constrained decoding reports improved executability in structured domains (e.g., cheminformatics), but those gains are domain‑dependent and contingent on tooling fidelity [11],[52].

Generate→validate→repair architectures and deterministic digital‑twin validators have been proposed and evaluated for NetOps and adjacent settings; published system papers and benchmarks show these pipelines can reduce observable errors under controlled scenarios, but measured magnitudes vary with validator coverage, repair budget, and evaluation design [5],[6],[7]. Crucially, many prior evaluations conflate downstream verifier effects with independent changes in generation (distinct prompts or decoding strategies). That conflation complicates causal attribution of observed gains to the validator/repair component alone. The literature therefore motivates experiments that hold generation constant while measuring only downstream validator/repair marginal returns [5],[7].

Agentic and multi‑stage NetOps architectures stress governance, protocol‑mediated execution, and proof-carrying traces as complements to any single model's behavior; these works argue that operational reliability depends on validator fidelity and orchestration policies rather than solely on the LLM [8],[9],[10]. Our study complements these lines by enforcing shared_initial_candidate semantics and measuring the isolated effect of a deterministic validator with a bounded single repair invocation — answering the precise causal estimand baseline initial validity versus final guarded validity after deterministic validation and permitted repair.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and confirmatory design. The study was preregistered as cand‑003‑stud‑001 and specified a paired binary design with task_count = 1,000 complete pairs, generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate, initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1, maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1, primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline, and primary confirmatory test = exact two‑sided McNemar. The paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) was prespecified as a descriptive summary. Independent_condition_generation was explicitly false in the frozen preregistration; no independent first‑pass generations for alternate prompts or decoding strategies were executed. These choices were fixed before any hosted‑model calls and enforced by the registered executor.

Task corpus and selection. Tasks derive from the synthetic challenging_workflow_stress_v1 corpus and were deterministically selected according to the preregistered index rule to yield 1,000 unique intents. Each task specifies initial_state, expected_final_state, required_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, and a difficulty annotation (including levels 'very_hard' and 'extreme'). Representative workflow patterns include safe_access_service_transfer, failover_then_offline_reconfiguration, rolling_access_vlan_migration, and composed_redundancy_and_access_maintenance; these patterns expose ordering and transient invariants that the validator enforces.

Adapter, model configuration, and validator semantics. The adapter family was hosted_netops_gvr_v1; declared provider/model was gpt‑5‑mini (provider: openai_responses). The recorded model_configuration shows temperature = null/unset; as preregistered we state explicitly that null/unset is not evidence of deterministic hosted‑model sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. Exactly one sampled initial generation per task was deterministically reused by both arms under shared_initial_candidate semantics. The guarded arm then applies deterministic validator checks via deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (a digital‑twin emulator that parses candidate command sequences and checks required command presence/order, protected-field noninterference, and workflow invariants); the validator emits a binary safe‑deploy decision and structured traces (validation_before, repair_applied, validation_after). If the validator rejects the initial candidate it may invoke at most one repair call; repair generation is recorded and revalidated.

Causal interpretation and analysis plan. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics the baseline outcome equals the initial single‑shot validity of the shared candidate while the guarded outcome equals final validity after deterministic validation and any permitted single repair. Because both arms begin from the identical initial sample, any discordant outcome (n10 or n01) can only arise from deterministic validator decision differences and/or validator‑triggered repair. The preregistered primary inference is the exact two‑sided McNemar test applied to paired counts (n_11, n_10, n_01, n_00); the preregistered paired bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) is reported as a descriptive summary computed by the registered executor.
sections.results:
Execution accounting. Planned episodes = 2,000; completed = 2,000; complete_pairs = 1,000; failed episodes = 0. Provider call audit: hosted model call event count = 1,005 comprising 1,000 shared initial generations and 5 repair invocations (stage counts recorded in the deterministic reconciliation artifact).

Primary paired outcomes (preregistered). Contingency counts: n11 = 995 (both succeeded), n10 = 5 (guarded succeeded, baseline failed), n01 = 0 (baseline succeeded, guarded failed), n00 = 0 (both failed). Observed success rates: baseline = 995/1000 = 0.995; guarded = 1000/1000 = 1.000; paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. Exact two‑sided McNemar p = 0.0625 (prespecified confirmatory test; α = 0.05: not significant per preregistered decision rule).

Paired bootstrap descriptive summary. The preregistered paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) computed by the registered executor is [0.001, 0.01]. This descriptive interval excludes zero in this run despite the confirmatory p‑value exceeding 0.05; this behavior is consistent with discreteness effects when discordant counts are extremely sparse.

Repair mechanics and failure diagnostics. Exactly five validator‑triggered repairs occurred and produced the five discordant improvements. Archived validator traces for repaired pairs document rejection of the shared initial candidate for rule‑level violations (notably ordering violations in required_sequence and unauthorized touches of protected interfaces), a single repair generation, and subsequent revalidation that accepted the repaired candidate. Repaired episodes are concentrated among higher‑difficulty patterns annotated 'very_hard' or 'extreme' and involve multi‑step required_sequence constraints. Total hosted model calls = 1,005 (1,000 shared initial + 5 repair) and all deterministic reconciliation checks passed.

Compact accounting summary. Planned episodes = 2,000; completed = 2,000; complete pairs = 1,000; model calls used = 1,005; repair calls invoked = 5; baseline successes = 995; guarded successes = 1,000; paired difference = 0.005; exact two‑sided McNemar p = 0.0625; paired bootstrap 95% CI = [0.001, 0.01] (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729).
sections.discussion:
Interpretation of confirmatory and descriptive evidence. The preregistered confirmatory decision uses the exact two‑sided McNemar (p = 0.0625); under the preregistered two‑sided α = 0.05 the study does not claim confirmatory evidence for a nonzero paired increase. The preregistered bootstrap CI ([0.001, 0.01]) is a descriptive summary produced by the registered executor and aids interpretation but does not supersede the prespecified confirmatory rule. Sparse discordant counts (n10 + n01 = 5) concentrate the null distribution for exact paired tests on a few small symmetric outcomes; two‑sided exact p‑values can therefore remain above 0.05 while resampling‑based percentile intervals exclude zero. This is a sampling‑distribution phenomenon arising from discreteness, not a contradiction in the recorded counts.

Power, ceiling effects, and design sensitivity. The preregistered power calculation assumed baseline≈0.60 and targeted an absolute increase of 0.15; under those assumptions task_count = 1,000 provided >80% power for the McNemar-style test. Observed baseline = 0.995 departs substantially from that assumption and concentrates mass in the concordant success cell (n11 = 995), leaving only five discordant pairs to inform inference. Detecting the observed tiny absolute increase (0.005) against a near‑unity baseline therefore requires either much larger paired sample sizes or design changes that increase discordant prevalence (for example, independent generation arms, injected failure cases, or a larger allowed repair budget). We therefore interpret the null confirmatory result in the context of a mismatch between preregistered operating assumptions and the observed operating point.

Failure‑mode patterns and construct implications. Archived validator traces show repaired cases share rule‑level failure modes: command ordering violations in required_sequence and unauthorized touches of protected interfaces. These failures concentrate in complex multi‑step workflows (cataloged patterns include safe_access_service_transfer, composed_redundancy_and_access_maintenance, and rolling_access_vlan_migration). The qualitative consistency of these modes supports the view that dependency and ordering constraints generate the long‑tail of repairable misconfigurations; however, with only five repairs we cannot estimate per-pattern repair efficacy precisely. This limits generalization of per-pattern repair rates but supports the narrower, evidence-grounded statement that the deterministic validator plus single repair averted a small number of unsafe initial candidates concentrated in higher‑difficulty workflows.

Design tradeoffs and operational implications. The shared_initial_candidate paired design intentionally isolates downstream validator and single‑repair marginal effects and avoids confounding with prompt/decoding or sampling interventions; this yields a precise causal estimand but precludes measuring generator‑level effects. The deterministic digital‑twin validator provides reproducible rule‑based adjudication but its coverage determines construct validity: missing semantic checks would reduce observed failures. Artifact‑grounded evidence therefore supports the practical conclusion that deterministic validator+single repair can avert some unsafe outcomes in synthetic NetOps workflows, but measurable marginal gains are small when baseline outputs are already highly valid and when the repair budget is constrained. Stated operational implications are hypotheses to be validated in follow‑up runs rather than empirical claims about production deployments.

Concrete follow‑ups (preregistered or documented in the archived manifest). (1) Execute independent first‑pass generation arms to measure generator+validator interactions (preregistered but not run here). (2) Sweep repair budgets (k > 1) to quantify marginal returns per additional repair call. (3) Expand validator rule suites and inject targeted failure cases to increase discordant prevalence and probe external validity. (4) Evaluate multiple model families and prompt/configuration variants. Each follow‑up should prespecify expected baseline failure ranges and adjust power calculations to the operating regime of interest.

Threats to validity. Construct validity depends on validator rule coverage; omitted semantic checks undercount failures. Internal validity: shared_initial_candidate correctly isolates downstream effects but prevents evaluation of generator interventions. External validity: synthetic corpus and single declared model (gpt‑5‑mini) limit generalization to heterogeneous production environments. Conclusion validity: near‑unity baseline produced sparse discordant counts and discrete p‑value behavior, reducing sensitivity for detecting small absolute effects. These limitations were prespecified and are documented in the archived manifest.
sections.conclusion: In a preregistered paired study with shared_initial_candidate semantics on a 1,000‑task synthetic NetOps stress corpus, a guarded generate→validate→repair pipeline produced a small absolute paired improvement (0.005) relative to a baseline single‑shot generator; the preregistered exact two‑sided McNemar did not meet two‑sided α = 0.05 (p = 0.0625). Only five validator repairs were invoked and total hosted model calls recorded = 1,005. The preregistered confirmatory result is the exact McNemar outcome; the paired bootstrap CI and other descriptive summaries are reported as preregistered secondary outputs. Artifact‑grounded evidence indicates downstream validator/repair safeguards can prevent some unsafe outcomes in structured NetOps workflows, but measurable marginal gains are constrained when baseline outputs are already highly valid and when the paired design intentionally isolates downstream effects. Follow‑ups that vary generator semantics, repair budgets, validator coverage, and model families are necessary to map marginal returns in realistic operating regimes.

Orchestration and validator: hosted_netops_gvr_v1 with deterministic_netops_validator_v5 as the validator/digital twin. Preregistration: study cand‑003‑stud‑001 (frozen prior to any model calls and recorded in the archived execution manifest). Immutable initial master prompt reference archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Model configuration recorded temperature = null/unset (null/unset does not imply deterministic sampling or temperature = 0). Human role and autonomy boundary: after the autonomy lock the research run executed the preregistered experiment, analysis, and manuscript drafting; no human manually edited the manuscript technical content after the autonomy lock.
limitations: Single‑model scope: only the declared model gpt‑5‑mini was evaluated; results do not generalize across model families or versions.

Synthetic corpus and deterministic validator: tasks come from a synthetic stress corpus and validation used a deterministic digital twin (deterministic_netops_validator_v5); external validity to heterogeneous vendor/legacy environments is limited.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics: the paired comparison isolates downstream validator/repair effects only; it does not measure differences that would arise from independent first‑pass generations or alternative prompting arms that were not executed (those arms were not part of the frozen preregistration).

Low baseline failure prevalence: baseline success = 99.5%; the preregistered power plan assumed baseline≈0.60 and a target effect of 0.15, so the observed baseline greatly reduces sensitivity to detect small absolute gains. This mismatch is reported explicitly and reduces the study's ability to detect very small practical effects using the preregistered confirmatory test.
Sparse repairs and interpretation limits: only five validator repairs were invoked, constraining inference about repair efficacy across failure modes.

Statistical nuance: the preregistered primary test is exact two‑sided McNemar (p = 0.0625). The paired bootstrap percentile CI [0.001, 0.01] is a preregistered descriptive summary but is sensitive to sparse discordant counts; a one‑sided McNemar (p = 0.03125) was computed post‑hoc and is explicitly labeled exploratory because it was not prespecified in the frozen preregistration.

Construct validity: the safe‑deploy binary depends on the emulator/validator's rule set; semantic and emergent multi‑device policy violations may be underrepresented in the validator's modeled constraints.
